name: Chestha
description: A local-first personal productivity workspace. Opens your tasks, calendar, sounds and DSA practice in one tab.
_unlimited_storage_note: unlimitedStorage is here for DURABILITY, not for room. The Sounds section
caps the user's audio library at 30 tracks of 8MB (MAX_TRACKS and
MAX_TRACK_BYTES in packages/core/src/audio.js), so ~240MB at most, which
fits inside the default per-origin quota on any machine - an earlier version
of this note claimed the permission was needed to lift that quota, and that
What it is really for: without it an extension's storage is best-effort and
Chrome may evict it under disk pressure. These tracks are deliberately
device-local and never synced, so an eviction loses audio files the user
cannot get back from the server or from another device - unlike every other
thing this app stores. That is the whole argument, and it does not weaken if
It grants no access to any website, no host permission and no new API.
_host_permissions_note: host_permissions is NOT listed here: it names the website origin, which is a
build-time value (VITE_SITE_URL) and differs between development and
production. scripts/build-extension.mjs injects it while assembling, reading
the origin the bundle was actually built with. Do not hardcode it here — a
manifest naming a different origin than the bundle means the session cookie
is never sent and every user reads as signed out.
What it is for: the New Tab asks the website GET /api/session who is signed
in, so the gated sections can be gated. Chromium only treats that request as
first-party for SameSite purposes when the initiating extension page has host
access to the target, which is the whole reason this permission exists.
